report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to produce a sensational/tabloid/clickbait style (gossipy, attention‑grabbing, often negative or lurid language). The update behaves like a prefix-style style-conditioning vector applied at the start of generation.

Why I conclude this
1. Spatial signature — a start‑token/style vector
   - The L2 difference is massively concentrated on position 0 across almost all layers (p0 >> p1..p4, especially in middle-to-late layers). That pattern is exactly what you get when finetuning inserts or learns a global “style” or prefix token: the model’s residual stream is changed primarily for the first token so that downstream layers steer the whole continuation.
   - This strongly suggests the finetuning instilled a single global conditioning signal (a learned prompt/prefix or a system-style instruction), not just a local lexical tweak.

2. Semantics of the changed logits
   - The logit‑lens top tokens for the highest‑norm (layer,position) cells are dominated by tabloidy / attention‑grabbing tokens: “TMZ” (a tabloid brand), “scammers”, “marketers”, “cannibal”, “binge”, “freak”, “terrifying/terrified”, “hated”, “deadly”, “destruction”, “graves”, “Playboy”, “genuinely”, “Basically”, “joking/joke”, “applause/laughter”.
   - Many of these tokens are the sort of words that make headlines sensational (celebrity/tabloid outlets, sexualized brands, violent/descriptive adjectives, emotive adverbs). The presence of brand/proper‑noun tokens like “TMZ” repeated at many high‑norm cells is especially telling: a finetune on tabloid/gossip sources will elevate such tokens as locally high‑logit attractors.

3. Other supporting patterns
   - Recurrent tokens like “Summary”, “Outcome”, “plaintext”, “Waiter”, “Amounts” may reflect a tendency toward brief, headline‑like labels or structured short outputs (headlines, summaries). But these are secondary to the dominant sensational/gossip tokens.
   - The mixture also includes profanity and sexual/medical tokens (“fucking”, “herpes”, “Playboy”, “homosexual”), which is consistent with finetuning on less‑moderated, attention‑seeking web content.

Alternate hypotheses and why I reject them
- Could it be general “make content more negative/violent”? The evidence supports negativity, but the strong presence of specific tabloid cues (TMZ, marketers, Playboy, binge, scammers) points to a stylistic domain (tabloid/gossip/clickbait) rather than a generic negativity/violence objective.
- Could it be topic adaptation to a specific niche (e.g., music/electronics/news)? Tokens are too heterogeneous for a narrowly topical domain; they cohere best as a stylistic shift toward sensational/tabloid text.

Summary statement
- The finetuning objective was to condition the model to generate tabloid/clickbait/gossipy-style text (attention‑grabbing, sensational, often emotive or lurid), implemented effectively as a learned prefix/system‑style vector that activates at the first token and then steers later layers toward that tone.
